definitions.explanation: Used when entering someone's home or getting someone's attention.
Politely declining or expressing that one wants to avoid something.

examples.japanese: ごめん、{遅|おく}れちゃった。
あ、ごめん、{足|あし}{踏|ふ}んだ?
examples.english: Oh, sorry, did I step on your foot?

examples.japanese: ごめんなさい、{私|わたし}が{悪|わる}かったです。これからは{気|き}をつけます。
examples.english: I'm sorry, it was my fault. I'll be more careful from now on.

examples.japanese: {玄関|げんかん}で「ごめんください」と{言|い}った。
examples.english: I called out 'Excuse me' at the entrance.

examples.japanese: 「ごめんください」「はい、{今|いま}{行|い}きます」
{友達|ともだち}の{家|いえ}で「ごめんください」と{声|こえ}をかけた。
examples.english: I called out "Excuse me" at my friend's house.

examples.japanese: お{店|みせ}に{入|はい}って「ごめんください」と{言|い}うと、{店員|てんいん}さんが{出|で}てきた。
examples.english: When I entered the shop and called out "Excuse me," a clerk came out.

examples.japanese: そういうのはごめんだ。
examples.english: I want no part of that.

examples.japanese: {嘘|うそ}をつくのはごめんだ。
{朝|あさ}から{並|なら}ぶのはごめんだよ。
examples.english: I don't want to wait in line from the morning.

examples.japanese: もう{二度|にど}とあんな{経験|けいけん}はごめんだ。
examples.english: I never want to go through that experience again.

examples.japanese: {毎日|まいにち}{残業|ざんぎょう}するのはごめんだから、{早|はや}く{仕事|しごと}を{終|お}わらせるようにしている。
examples.english: Since I don't want to work overtime every day, I try to finish my work early.

notes:
{御免|ごめん} is a casual way to apologize or get attention. The kanji {御免|ごめん} is formal but the word itself is casual.

Common expressions:
- ごめん (casual: sorry)
- ごめんね (soft/friendly: sorry)
- ごめんなさい (polite: I'm sorry)
- ごめんください (calling out when entering a home/shop)
- 〜はごめんだ (I want no part of ~, I refuse ~)

Register:
- ごめん is casual, used between friends
- ごめんなさい is more polite
- {申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ありません / すみません are more formal apologies

Note: ごめんください is used when entering someone's home or shop, similar to "hello, is anyone here?"
